action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves from 0.5 mm to 3.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Perform a bedside ice-pack test on the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable left ptosis is present; an improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling supports a neuromuscular junction cause and costs nothing.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding, blocking, modulating and MuSK antibodies negative at the reference laboratory; TSH and free T4 normal
action_criteria.label: Repeat AChR and MuSK antibodies with thyroid function at the reference laboratory
action_criteria.rationale: The outside double-negative result is the basis of the functional label; confirming it at a reference laboratory and adding thyroid function, never checked, is the first step before extended serology (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No significant decrement (maximum 9% in trapezius), normal baseline CMAPs and no significant post-exercise increment
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation including facial, trapezius and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: RNS of weak facial and proximal muscles is the first electrodiagnostic test and also screens for LEMS through baseline CMAPs and post-exercise increment (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-LRP4 antibody positive by cell-based assay (titre 1:400); clustered AChR negative
action_criteria.label: Order LRP4 antibody testing in this double-seronegative patient
action_criteria.rationale: With fatigable ptosis, diplopia and bulbar symptoms and negative AChR and MuSK antibodies, the extended cell-based panel (LRP4, clustered AChR) is the next serological step (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance; Evoli 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter and blocking in extensor digitorum communis (MCD 58 us) and orbicularis oculi (MCD 47 us)
action_criteria.label: Order single-fibre EMG of a limb and a facial muscle
action_criteria.rationale: RNS is normal and the patient is double seronegative, so SFEMG is the study that demonstrates the transmission defect; it is abnormal in over 90% of MG but is not specific (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No thymoma; fatty-replaced involuted thymus; mild emphysema
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast
action_criteria.rationale: Thymic imaging is indicated in every patient with MG regardless of serostatus; a thymoma would change management (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 3.8 L (84% predicted, 43.8 mL/kg), MIP -72 cmH2O, MEP 112 cmH2O: no respiratory muscle weakness
action_criteria.label: Measure baseline respiratory function
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar symptoms (chewing fatigue, dysarthria) with sleep apnoea: baseline FVC, MIP and MEP stage respiratory reserve before treatment (Lawn 2001 thresholds).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction of pyridostigmine with lisinopril; statins carry rare reports of MG worsening
action_criteria.label: Optionally check his medications against the MG treatment
action_criteria.rationale: Lisinopril and atorvastatin have no interaction that changes the plan; the statin caution is a monitoring point.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on seronegative and LRP4-positive MG
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on seronegative MG
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to a functional cause on the basis of negative AChR and MuSK antibodies; seronegative MG needs extended serology and single-fibre EMG.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.

Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.
Do not add a beta-blocker if his blood pressure treatment needs intensifying; choose another class.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30-60 mg three to five times daily, titrated to effect (maximum about 360-480 mg/day).

If bulbar and ocular symptoms persist on pyridostigmine, start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase slowly; add azathioprine after TPMT testing if long-term immunosuppression is needed (Sanders 2016).
Replace the functional diagnosis in his record with LRP4-antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis and explain the diagnosis to him and his GP.

Give him a list of drugs that can worsen MG (fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium, beta-blockers), keep atorvastatin under review if weakness worsens, and advise urgent review for dysphagia or breathlessness.

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or encephalopathy; EEG has no role in a neuromuscular junction disorder (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
No CNS or inflammatory neuropathy question; CSF has no role in MG (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
FDG-PET is not indicated in MG; contrast CT answers the thymic question.
No cardiac symptom or sign; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: LRP4 antibody-positive myasthenia gravis, generalized (double-seronegative for AChR and MuSK)

differential.key_features: The prior label rested on double-negative serology; objective fatigable ptosis, a positive ice-pack test, abnormal SFEMG jitter and blocking and a positive LRP4 antibody exclude it.
MuSK antibody negative on repeat RIA at the reference laboratory; LRP4 antibody explains the seronegative disease.
AChR binding, blocking and modulating antibodies negative twice, and clustered AChR negative by cell-based assay.
Normal baseline CMAPs, no significant post-exercise increment, normal reflexes, no autonomic symptoms and prominent ocular signs; chest CT shows no lung mass.
Onset at 48 with no childhood symptoms or family history, and an autoantibody (LRP4) that explains the disease.
Ptosis is fatigable, diurnal and ice-pack positive, and there is no fixed ophthalmoplegia.

key_clinical_evidence: Fatigable left-predominant ptosis, diplopia on sustained gaze, chewing fatigue and dysarthria on counting, worse in the evening, point to a neuromuscular junction disorder despite the prior functional label.
Positive ice-pack test on the left (MRD1 0.5 to 3.5 mm).
AChR and MuSK antibodies are negative on repeat testing, so the extended cell-based panel is needed: anti-LRP4 is positive at 1:400 and clustered AChR is negative.
RNS is normal (maximum decrement 9%), which does not exclude MG; SFEMG shows increased jitter and blocking in extensor digitorum communis and orbicularis oculi.
Mediastinal CT shows an involuted thymus without thymoma; thymectomy is not routine in LRP4-positive MG outside trials.
Respiratory function is normal (FVC 84% predicted, 43.8 mL/kg; MIP -72 cmH2O).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Double seronegativity does not exclude MG; extended cell-based serology (LRP4, clustered AChR) and SFEMG are the next steps.
red_herrings.data_point: Anti-AChR binding, blocking, modulating negative; Anti-MuSK negative (double-seronegative)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude that MG is excluded on the basis of double-negative conventional serology and anchor toward functional or psychogenic diagnosis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: RNS is normal in a substantial minority of generalized MG and more often in seronegative disease; a normal RNS calls for SFEMG rather than excluding MG.
red_herrings.data_point: Normal repetitive nerve stimulation study (maximum decrement 9%, below 10% threshold)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude that electrophysiology excludes MG and reinforce functional attribution, particularly in combination with the negative serology.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A functional label requires positive functional signs and an organic work-up; the MG work-up was incomplete without extended serology and SFEMG.
red_herrings.data_point: Prior clinician attribution to 'stress and fatigue' and CBT referral without completing MG workup (no LRP4, no SFEMG)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on the established functional label and defer further neurological workup, particularly in a male patient with occupational stress.

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
LRP4 and clustered AChR cell-based testing follows negative AChR and MuSK antibodies (Jacob 2025).

labs.interpretation: Anti-AChR binding, blocking and modulating antibodies and anti-MuSK antibody not detected. Thyroid function, CBC, BMP and CK within reference ranges. A negative AChR or MuSK antibody result does not exclude a disorder of neuromuscular transmission; clinical correlation recommended.

seronegative myasthenia gravis diagnosis.query: seronegative myasthenia gravis diagnosis and management

results.finding: Pyridostigmine is the initial symptomatic treatment; corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy are used when treatment goals are not met. Thymectomy may be considered in seronegative generalized MG that does not respond to immunotherapy.
results.source: Sanders DB et al. Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al. Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: Antibodies to LRP4, the agrin receptor that activates MuSK, were found in a subset of patients with MG seronegative for AChR and MuSK antibodies.
results.source: Higuchi O et al. Ann Neurol 2011;69:418-422

results.finding: LRP4 antibody frequency among double-seronegative patients varied widely between countries; LRP4-positive patients often had mild generalized or ocular disease.
results.source: Zisimopoulou P et al. J Autoimmun 2014;52:139-145

seronegative myasthenia gravis diagnosis.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122) recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fibre EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma. LRP4 antibodies are found in a minority of patients seronegative for AChR and MuSK, with frequencies that vary between cohorts (Higuchi O et al., Ann Neurol 2011; Zisimopoulou P et al., J Autoimmun 2014).

patient.chief_complaint: Fluctuating drooping left eyelid and double vision, attributed to 'stress and fatigue' for 4 months

family_history: No family history of neuromuscular disease

social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago (10 pack-years)

patient.history_present_illness:
A 48-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, and obstructive sleep apnoea presented to the neurology inpatient service for evaluation of progressive, fluctuating left ptosis and diplopia over 4 months. He initially noticed intermittent left eyelid drooping when driving home after long shifts, which he attributed to fatigue from work and disrupted sleep. His wife noted that the drooping was consistently worse in the evening and absent in the morning. Over the following 6 weeks, he developed horizontal diplopia during sustained lateral gaze, and jaw fatigue when chewing through a full meal. He also began experiencing slurred speech after prolonged speaking, typically after more than 30-40 minutes of telephone calls. His primary care physician initially attributed symptoms to work-related stress and referred him for sleep optimisation and CPAP pressure adjustment. His CPAP download showed good adherence with a residual AHI below 5. His symptoms did not improve. He was then evaluated by ophthalmology, who found no structural orbital pathology and measured intraocular pressure as normal; they noted the left ptosis was variable across the visit and referred to neurology.

At a neurology outpatient visit two months prior to this admission, AChR binding and blocking antibodies were checked and returned negative; MuSK antibodies were checked 3 weeks later at an outside laboratory and also returned negative. The treating neurologist interpreted the double-negative result as 'essentially excluding myasthenia gravis' and attributed his symptoms to a functional/psychogenic overlay in the context of occupational stress. The patient was referred to psychology. He completed 6 weeks of CBT-based sessions without benefit and was subsequently admitted for inpatient evaluation after his wife witnessed visible ptosis and slurred speech at dinner and called the neurology team.

He denied any limb weakness at rest, sensory disturbance, headache, weight loss, night sweats, cough, or haemoptysis. He denied use of aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, or any new medications. His symptoms are consistently worse later in the day and dramatically improved after one hour of rest, which he initially attributed to recovering from fatigue. He has no history of thyroid disease.

neurological_exam.additional: No dysphagia at rest; patient reports difficulty finishing large meals ('tires out chewing') over the past 2 months. Voice quality hoarse at the end of the day.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left ptosis: MRD1 2.5 mm at rest, falling to 0.5 mm after 90 seconds of sustained upgaze (fatigable ptosis, left > right). Faint right ptosis on prolonged testing. No diplopia at rest; horizontal diplopia on sustained lateral gaze after 45 seconds. Cogan lid twitch sign absent. Pupils 3 mm, equal, reactive, no RAPD. Mild dysarthria on counting to 50 (slurring at counts 35-50). Tongue strength mildly reduced bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. No facial weakness at rest.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Normal language. No cognitive impairment.
neurological_exam.motor: Deltoid strength 4+/5 bilaterally at rest, declining to 4-/5 after 10 repetitions of sustained abduction (objective fatigability). Neck flexors 4+/5. Grip strength 5/5 and non-fatigable. No lower extremity weakness. No fasciculations.
neurological_exam.reflexes: DTRs 2+ throughout. Bilateral plantar flexor response.

physical_exam.general: Weight 86.8 kg, height 178 cm. Well appearing, no respiratory distress.
